**Suite run 1 (the branch as it stood at it.236, no changes yet):** 1 failed, 183 passed, 1 skipped in 585.97 s (`/tmp/loop-ancient-works.a/fullsuite-237.log`). All four a423d19 reds green (matchfit 2/2; owner_check pair green; test_merge, test_data, serve, all src_ tests green). The single red: tests/test_src_roman_maclauchlan.py::test_check_staged_joins_and_passes at step (a): `join: staged site luguvallium-q71551754 differs from its canonical row in extras.jsonl` (check_staged() returned 1, `assert 1 == 0`). Not in the a423d19 failure list and not in any loop-start note, so a NEW failure on this branch - and, being a date-bomb, unfixable by waiting (it reds on every day after the merge date).

**Root cause (measured, not guessed):** the test's first step re-runs the book's stage() into temp files (offline), then check_staged() joins the freshly staged row against the REAL canonical files (monkeypatched to temp copies of them only in steps b/c). stage() built the site row with `"checked": now()` and the picture row with `evidence: {"checked": now(), ...}` where `now()` = `time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` = the run date. The committed staging rows (207b, staged 2026-10-14) and the canonical rows 230 merged from them (byte-identical copies) carry 2026-10-14 - the day the LIVE verification actually ran: the P625 cross-check ("(verified 2026-10-14)") and the sitelinks check (the note field hard-codes "(sitelinks checked 2026-10-14)"). A fresh re-stage on 2026-10-15 re-stamps both fields to 2026-10-15; the join normalizes FULL row content (`_canon_norm` = same norm fit/merge.py uses on the merge line), so the fresh row differs from the merged row in exactly two date fields (verified by walking the fresh-vs-canonical row diff: only `location_check.checked` and `evidence.checked` differ) -> "differs" -> exit 1. The test passed in a423d19 only because that run was on 2026-10-14, the same date as the staging/merge -> identical rows. The test itself is correct and was NOT touched: case (b) is exactly the intended post-merge contract ("a merged row is a no-op"), and only a deterministic staging date can satisfy it on later days. An offline re-stage that has not re-run the live checks must not claim a new verification date - that is what re-stamping does, and it is a false record under the 200 evidence contract either way.
